name: Single-Arm Cable Lateral Raise
summary: An isolation exercise that uses a low cable pulley to provide continuous tension across the shoulder during lateral abduction.

setup: Set the cable pulley to its lowest position or around mid-shin height and attach a single D-handle.
Stand with the working side turned away from the cable tower, or position the cable so the line of pull crosses in front of or behind your body.
Grasp the handle with the outside hand and hold the cable upright or machine frame with the non-working hand for stability.
Stand tall with a slight bend in your working elbow and a stable hip-width stance.
steps: Raise your working arm out to the side in the scapular plane until your hand is roughly level with your shoulder.
Pause briefly at the top to accentuate the contraction in the lateral deltoid.
Lower the handle smoothly along the same arc back toward the starting position, resisting the cable's pull.
Complete the target repetitions, then switch sides and repeat.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you raise the cable out to your side; inhale smoothly as you lower it under control.
cues: Pour the water at the top

common_faults.fault: Swinging the torso or using hip momentum to initiate the raise.
common_faults.correction: Hold the machine tower with the free hand, brace the core, and select a lighter weight that allows pure shoulder abduction.

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the shoulder excessively with the upper trapezius.
common_faults.correction: Keep your shoulder blade depressed and think of reaching outward toward the wall rather than straight upward.

common_faults.fault: Bending and extending the elbow dynamically during the rep.
common_faults.correction: Lock a slight, comfortable bend in your elbow from start to finish so the movement occurs solely at the shoulder joint.

precautions: Avoid raising the arm higher than shoulder height if you experience impingement or shoulder pain.
